nodes.name: Generative model with continuous latent variables
nodes.statement: A two-step random process generating dataset $\bX = \{\bx^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^N$: latent $\bz^{(i)} \sim p_{\bT^*}(\bz)$, then $\bx^{(i)} \sim p_{\bT^*}(\bx|\bz)$, with PDFs differentiable a.e. in $\bT$ and $\bz$.
nodes.statement_clean: Directed model with continuous latent variable z generating x, with parametric prior and likelihood differentiable in parameters and latents.

nodes.name: Recognition model (probabilistic encoder)
nodes.statement: An approximate posterior $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ that approximates the intractable true posterior $p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx)$; not necessarily factorial; parameters $\bphi$ learned jointly with $\bT$.
nodes.statement_clean: Encoder distribution q_phi(z|x) approximating the intractable posterior, learned jointly with the generative model.

nodes.name: Probabilistic decoder
nodes.statement: The conditional generative distribution $p_{\bT}(\bx|\bz)$, which given a latent code $\bz$ produces a distribution over corresponding values of $\bx$.

nodes.name: Variational lower bound (ELBO)
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) = \mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)}[-\log q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx) + \log p_{\bT}(\bx,\bz)] = -D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})\,\|\,p_{\bT}(\bz)) + \mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})}[\log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz)]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lower bound on log marginal likelihood, equal to negative KL from prior plus expected log likelihood under the approximate posterior.

nodes.name: Reparameterization of latent variable
nodes.statement: Express $\tilde{\bz} \sim q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ as $\tilde{\bz} = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$ with auxiliary noise $\beps \sim p(\beps)$, where $g_{\bphi}$ is a differentiable transformation.
nodes.statement_clean: Write the latent sample as a deterministic function of input and independent noise so that gradients pass through the sampling step.

nodes.name: Variational auto-encoder
nodes.statement: An instance of the AEVB algorithm in which the recognition model $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ is parameterized by a neural network (MLP) producing the mean and variance of a diagonal-covariance Gaussian over $\bz$.

nodes.name: Bernoulli MLP decoder
nodes.statement: $\log p(\bx|\bz) = \sum_{i=1}^D x_i \log y_i + (1-x_i)\log(1-y_i)$ with $\by = f_\sigma(\bW_2 \tanh(\bW_1 \bz + \bbb_1) + \bbb_2)$.

nodes.name: Gaussian MLP encoder/decoder
nodes.statement: $\log p(\bx|\bz) = \log \mathcal{N}(\bx;\bmu,\bsigma^2 \bI)$ with $\bmu = \bW_4 \bh + \bbb_4$, $\log \bsigma^2 = \bW_5 \bh + \bbb_5$, $\bh = \tanh(\bW_3 \bz + \bbb_3)$.

nodes.name: Naive score-function gradient estimator
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{\bphi} \mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz)}[f(\bz)] = \mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz)}[f(\bz) \nabla_{q_{\bphi}(\bz)} \log q_{\bphi}(\bz)]$ — known to have very high variance.
nodes.origin_citation: Blei et al. 2012; Ranganath et al. 2013

nodes.name: Generic SGVB estimator (estimator A)
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^A(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) = \frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)},\bz^{(i,l)}) - \log q_{\bphi}(\bz^{(i,l)}|\bx^{(i)})$, $\bz^{(i,l)} = g_{\bphi}(\bepsilon^{(i,l)},\bx^{(i)})$.

nodes.name: KL-form SGVB estimator (estimator B)
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^B(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) = -D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})\,\|\,p_{\bT}(\bz)) + \frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(i,l)})$, with the KL term integrated analytically when possible.

nodes.name: Minibatch SGVB estimator
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bX) \simeq \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^M(\bT,\bphi;\bX^M) = \frac{N}{M} \sum_{i=1}^M \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)})$ for a random minibatch $\bX^M$ of size $M$.

nodes.name: Gaussian-Gaussian KL closed form
nodes.statement: $-D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz)\,\|\,p_{\bT}(\bz)) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^J \big(1 + \log(\sigma_j^2) - \mu_j^2 - \sigma_j^2 \big)$ when prior and posterior approximation are Gaussian with $p_{\bT}(\bz)=\mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$.

nodes.name: VAE Gaussian estimator
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)}) \simeq \frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^J(1 + \log((\sigma_j^{(i)})^2) - (\mu_j^{(i)})^2 - (\sigma_j^{(i)})^2) + \frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(i,l)})$, $\bz^{(i,l)} = \bmu^{(i)} + \bsigma^{(i)} \odot \bepsilon^{(l)}$.

nodes.name: Marginal likelihood estimator (importance form)
nodes.statement: $p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}) \simeq \big(\frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L \frac{q(\bz^{(l)})}{p_{\bT}(\bz)\,p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(l)})}\big)^{-1}$ with $\bz^{(l)} \sim p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})$ via HMC.

nodes.name: Efficient inference and learning in directed models with intractable posteriors
nodes.statement: Given i.i.d. data $\bX$ from $p_{\bT^*}(\bx) = \int p_{\bT^*}(\bz)p_{\bT^*}(\bx|\bz)\,d\bz$ with intractable marginal and posterior, compute (1) approximate ML/MAP estimate of $\bT$, (2) approximate posterior $p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx)$, (3) approximate marginal $p_{\bT}(\bx)$, scalably for large $N$.
nodes.statement_clean: Jointly do ML/MAP parameter learning and posterior/marginal inference in directed continuous-latent models with intractable integrals and large datasets.

nodes.name: High-variance score-function gradient
nodes.statement: Standard Monte Carlo (REINFORCE-style) gradient $\nabla_{\bphi} \mathbb{E}_{q_{\bphi}(\bz)}[f(\bz)]$ via the score function exhibits very high variance and is impractical for variational learning of $\bphi$.

nodes.name: Mild differentiability conditions for reparameterization
nodes.statement: The PDFs $p_{\bT}(\bz)$ and $p_{\bT}(\bx|\bz)$ are differentiable almost everywhere in $\bT$ and $\bz$, and $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ admits a differentiable reparameterization $\bz = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$ with $\beps \sim p(\beps)$ independent of $\bphi$.

nodes.name: Differentiable reparameterized expectation
nodes.statement: If $\bz = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$ with $\beps \sim p(\beps)$ independent of $\bphi$, then $\int q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx) f(\bz)\,d\bz = \int p(\beps) f(g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx))\,d\beps \simeq \frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L f(g_{\bphi}(\bx,\bepsilon^{(l)}))$, giving an estimator that is differentiable in $\bphi$.
conclusions: The Monte Carlo estimator $\frac{1}{L}\sum_l f(g_{\bphi}(\bx,\bepsilon^{(l)}))$ is differentiable in $\bphi$

nodes.name: Variational lower bound identity
nodes.statement: For any $q_{\bphi}$, $\log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}) = D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})\,\|\,p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})) + \mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)})$, hence $\log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}) \geq \mathcal{L}(\bT,\bphi;\bx^{(i)})$ (KL is non-negative).
assumptions: $p_{\bT}(\bx,\bz)$ is a joint density with marginal $p_{\bT}(\bx)$
$q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ is any density with the same support as $p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx)$

nodes.name: Closed-form Gaussian KL term
nodes.section: Appendix B (Solution of KL, Gaussian case)
nodes.statement: For $\pT(\bz) = \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$ and $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx^{(i)}) = \mathcal{N}(\bmu^{(i)},(\bsigma^{(i)})^2 \bI)$, $-D_{KL}(q_{\bphi}\,\|\,\pT(\bz)) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^J(1 + \log\sigma_j^2 - \mu_j^2 - \sigma_j^2)$.

nodes.name: Proof of reparameterized differentiable estimator
nodes.statement: Change of variables on $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)\prod_i dz_i = p(\beps)\prod_i d\epsilon_i$, then form a Monte Carlo estimate of the resulting integral over $p(\beps)$.

nodes.name: Derivation of the marginal likelihood estimator
nodes.statement: Multiply $1/p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)})$ by $\int q(\bz)\,d\bz$, rewrite as an expectation under the true posterior, and approximate by Monte Carlo with samples from HMC.

nodes.name: Derivation of Gaussian-Gaussian KL closed form
nodes.statement: Compute $\int q(\bz)\log p(\bz)\,d\bz$ and $\int q(\bz)\log q(\bz)\,d\bz$ for Gaussians with diagonal covariance and subtract.

nodes.name: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes (AEVB) algorithm
nodes.section: 2.3 The SGVB estimator and AEVB algorithm
nodes.statement: Stochastic-gradient procedure that jointly learns generative parameters $\bT$ and recognition parameters $\bphi$ by maximizing the SGVB lower bound on minibatches.
input: Recognition model $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ with reparameterization $\bz = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$, $\beps \sim p(\beps)$
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize $\bT,\bphi$; repeat: sample minibatch $\bX^M$, draw $\beps$, compute $\bg = \nabla_{\bT,\bphi} \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^M(\bT,\bphi;\bX^M,\beps)$, update $(\bT,\bphi)$ with SGD/Adagrad until convergence.

nodes.name: Full-VB stochastic-gradient procedure
nodes.statement: Stochastic-gradient procedure for the fully Bayesian extension that places a variational posterior $q_{\bphi}(\bT)$ over parameters in addition to $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$, both reparameterized.
output: Stochastic gradient $\bg$ of the variational lower bound w.r.t. $\bphi$
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize $\bg \gets 0$; for $l=1..L$: draw $\bx \sim \bX$, $\beps \sim p(\beps)$, $\bzeta \sim p(\bzeta)$; $\bg \mathrel{+}= \frac{1}{L}\nabla_{\bphi} f_{\bphi}(\bx, g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx), h_{\bphi}(\bzeta))$; return $\bg$.

nodes.name: Wake-Sleep algorithm
nodes.statement: Online learning algorithm for directed latent-variable models that alternates between wake-phase updates of the generative model and sleep-phase updates of the recognition model.

nodes.name: Monte Carlo EM with HMC
nodes.statement: EM-style algorithm that, instead of using an encoder, samples latents from the per-datapoint posterior using Hybrid Monte Carlo with leapfrog steps and then performs weight updates with Adagrad.
input: HMC step size and number of leapfrog steps
nodes.pseudocode: Per datapoint: run 10 HMC leapfrog steps with adaptive step size targeting 90% acceptance, then 5 weight updates using the obtained sample; repeat.

nodes.name: Univariate Gaussian reparameterization
nodes.statement: For $z \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$, take $z = \mu + \sigma\epsilon$ with $\epsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$; then $\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{N}(z;\mu,\sigma^2)}[f(z)] = \mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{N}(\epsilon;0,1)}[f(\mu+\sigma\epsilon)]$.

nodes.name: Variational Auto-Encoder on MNIST and Frey Face
nodes.statement: Train AEVB with MLP encoder/decoder ($500$ hidden units for MNIST, $200$ for Frey Face) using Adagrad, $M=100$, $L=1$; compare against wake-sleep and Monte Carlo EM on the variational lower bound and estimated marginal likelihood.
nodes.statement_clean: MNIST and Frey Face experiments comparing AEVB to wake-sleep and MCEM on lower bound and marginal likelihood.

nodes.name: 2D latent manifold visualization
nodes.statement: Train AEVB with $J=2$ latent dimensions and visualize the learned manifold by passing inverse-CDF-transformed grid points through the decoder for MNIST and Frey Face.

nodes.name: Full-VB Gaussian example
nodes.statement: With Gaussian prior on $\bT$ and $\bz$ and Gaussian variational posteriors, four terms of $f_{\bphi}$ collapse analytically, yielding a low-variance estimator combining two closed-form Gaussian-KL contributions and one Monte Carlo log-likelihood term.

nodes.name: Connection between AEVB and auto-encoders
nodes.statement: Estimator B can be read as auto-encoder objective: the KL term acts as a regularizer driving $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)$ toward the prior, and $\log p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(i,l)})$ is a negative reconstruction error.

nodes.name: Three families of reparameterizable distributions
nodes.statement: Differentiable transformations $g_{\bphi}$ exist when (i) the inverse CDF is tractable, (ii) the distribution is location-scale, or (iii) the variable is a composition of reparameterizable variates (Log-Normal, Gamma, Dirichlet, Beta, Chi-squared, F).

nodes.name: PCA as ML solution of linear-Gaussian generative model
nodes.statement: PCA arises as the maximum-likelihood solution of a linear-Gaussian model with $p(\bz) = \mathcal{N}(0,\bI)$ and $p(\bx|\bz) = \mathcal{N}(\bx;\bW \bz,\epsilon \bI)$ in the limit $\epsilon \to 0$.
nodes.origin_citation: Roweis 1998 (EM algorithms for PCA and SPCA)

nodes.name: Change-of-variables identity for $q_{\bphi}$
nodes.statement: Given $\bz = g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx)$, the densities transform as $q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx)\prod_i dz_i = p(\beps)\prod_i d\epsilon_i$.

nodes.name: Rewrite the expectation under $p(\beps)$
nodes.statement: Substitute the change-of-variables identity to get $\int q_{\bphi}(\bz|\bx) f(\bz)\,d\bz = \int p(\beps) f(g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx))\,d\beps$.

nodes.name: Form the Monte Carlo estimator
nodes.statement: Approximate the integral over $p(\beps)$ by sampling $\beps^{(l)} \sim p(\beps)$, giving $\frac{1}{L}\sum_{l=1}^L f(g_{\bphi}(\bx,\beps^{(l)}))$, which is differentiable in $\bphi$ since $\beps$ does not depend on $\bphi$.

nodes.name: Insert $\int q(\bz)\,d\bz = 1$
nodes.statement: Write $\frac{1}{p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)})} = \frac{\int q(\bz)\,d\bz}{p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)})}$ and multiply numerator and denominator by $p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)},\bz)$ inside the integral.

nodes.name: Identify true posterior
nodes.statement: Recognize $p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)},\bz)/p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}) = p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})$ to obtain $\int p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})\,\frac{q(\bz)}{p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)},\bz)}\,d\bz$.

nodes.name: Monte Carlo estimate via HMC
nodes.statement: Approximate the expectation by samples $\bz^{(l)} \sim p_{\bT}(\bz|\bx^{(i)})$ drawn with HMC, giving $\frac{1}{p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)})} \simeq \frac{1}{L}\sum_l \frac{q(\bz^{(l)})}{p_{\bT}(\bz)\,p_{\bT}(\bx^{(i)}|\bz^{(l)})}$ and invert.

nodes.name: Compute $\int q\log p$ for Gaussian prior
nodes.statement: $\int \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2) \log \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bzero,\bI)\,d\bz = -\frac{J}{2}\log(2\pi) - \frac{1}{2}\sum_j (\mu_j^2 + \sigma_j^2)$.

nodes.name: Compute $\int q\log q$ for Gaussian $q$
nodes.statement: $\int \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2)\log \mathcal{N}(\bz;\bmu,\bsigma^2)\,d\bz = -\frac{J}{2}\log(2\pi) - \frac{1}{2}\sum_j(1 + \log \sigma_j^2)$ (Gaussian differential entropy).

nodes.name: Subtract to obtain $-D_{KL}$
nodes.statement: Subtract the two integrals: $-D_{KL} = \int q(\log p - \log q) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_j(1 + \log\sigma_j^2 - \mu_j^2 - \sigma_j^2)$.

nodes.name: Initialize parameters
nodes.statement: $\bT,\bphi \gets$ initial values (e.g. random sampling from $\mathcal{N}(0,0.01)$).

nodes.name: Outer training loop
nodes.statement: Repeat the following stochastic-gradient updates until convergence of $(\bT,\bphi)$.

nodes.name: Sample minibatch
nodes.statement: $\bX^M \gets$ random minibatch of $M$ datapoints drawn from $\bX$.

nodes.name: Sample noise
nodes.statement: $\beps \gets$ random samples from noise distribution $p(\beps)$.

nodes.name: Compute SGVB gradient
nodes.statement: $\bg \gets \nabla_{\bT,\bphi} \widetilde{\mathcal{L}}^M(\bT,\bphi;\bX^M,\beps)$ using the minibatch SGVB estimator.

nodes.name: Update parameters
nodes.statement: $\bT,\bphi \gets$ stochastic-gradient update using $\bg$ (SGD or Adagrad).

nodes.name: Return parameters
nodes.statement: Return $\bT, \bphi$ at convergence.

nodes.name: Initialize accumulator
nodes.statement: $\bg \gets 0$.

nodes.name: Loop over $L$ Monte Carlo draws
nodes.statement: For $l=1,\dots,L$: draw $\bx \sim \bX$, $\beps \sim p(\beps)$, $\bzeta \sim p(\bzeta)$ and accumulate $\bg \mathrel{+}= \frac{1}{L}\nabla_{\bphi} f_{\bphi}(\bx, g_{\bphi}(\beps,\bx), h_{\bphi}(\bzeta))$.

nodes.name: Return gradient
nodes.statement: Return $\bg$, an unbiased stochastic gradient of the full-VB lower bound w.r.t. $\bphi$.
